definitions.explanation: Money deposited with the court to secure the temporary release of a person awaiting trial.

examples.japanese: {保釈金|ほしゃくきん}を{払|はら}った。
{保釈金|ほしゃくきん}は{一千万円|いっせんまんえん}に{設定|せってい}された。
examples.english: Bail was set at ten million yen.

examples.japanese: {被告人|ひこくにん}が{裁判|さいばん}に{出廷|しゅってい}しなかった{場合|ばあい}、{保釈金|ほしゃくきん}は{没収|ぼっしゅう}される。
examples.english: If the defendant fails to appear in court, the bail money is forfeited.

notes:
A compound of {保釈|ほしゃく} (bail/release on bail) and {金|きん} (money). In Japan, bail is granted much less frequently than in many Western countries. Japan's criminal justice system has a very high conviction rate, and suspects are often detained throughout the investigation and trial process. When bail is granted, the amounts can be substantial — often tens of millions of yen for serious cases.

The {保釈金|ほしゃくきん} is returned if the defendant complies with all bail conditions and appears for trial.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {保釈金|ほしゃくきん}を{納|おさ}める: to deposit bail money
- {保釈金|ほしゃくきん}が{没収|ぼっしゅう}される: for bail to be forfeited
- {保釈金|ほしゃくきん}の{返還|へんかん}: return of bail money

RELATED WORDS:
- {保釈|ほしゃく}: bail; release on bail
- {保釈|ほしゃく}される: to be released on bail
- {拘留|こうりゅう}: detention
- {勾留|こうりゅう}: pretrial detention
